whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Financial Services Cloud Accredited Professional exam for?

personas.label: Banking and wealth management consultants
personas.description: You set up Financial Services Cloud for banks, advisers or wealth firms and want to prove you know its data model.

personas.label: Salesforce admins at financial firms
personas.description: You run FSC day to day and want to understand households, financial accounts and rollups properly.

personas.label: Insurance and fintech implementation partners
personas.description: You deliver FSC projects and need a credential clients recognise.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Financial Services Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam, but FSC's data model is quite different from standard Salesforce. Once you understand how people, households and financial accounts link together, most questions get easier.
bullets: About 65% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current figure.
Data model focus. Person accounts, households, financial accounts, roles and relationships.
Industry features. Rollups, referrals, action plans, interaction summaries and compliant data sharing.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Set up a household with several members and financial accounts in a trial org, and check how the totals roll up. Before you book. Aim for 75% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Financial Services Cloud Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a client or adviser need, such as showing a family's total assets or passing a referral to a mortgage specialist, and ask which FSC feature fits.
bestWayToPass: Draw the data model: Person account, household, account-contact relationship, financial account and financial account role.
Understand rollups: How balances roll up from financial accounts to people and households.
Learn the adviser tools: Referrals, action plans, goals and interaction summaries.
Know the privacy features: Compliant data sharing and how it limits who sees client data.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up Financial Services Cloud: the client and household data model, financial accounts and rollups, referrals, action plans and compliance features. The exam is 50 scored questions in 75 minutes, with a 56% pass mark, weighted towards Delivery (46%) and Define/Design (42%).

keyConcepts.h2: Financial Services Cloud: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: FSC Data Model: Households, Individuals, and Financial Accounts
blocks.body: Individual clients are usually **person accounts**. A **household** is an account that groups people who manage money together, such as a family. People join a household through **account-contact relationships**, with one marked as the primary member. **Financial accounts** hold bank accounts, investments, loans and so on. **Financial account roles** link each financial account to the people involved, such as primary owner or joint owner. **Financial holdings** record what is inside an investment account, and **assets and liabilities** record things like a house or a mortgage held elsewhere.

blocks.heading: Relationship Management and Referrals
blocks.body: Advisers need to see who is connected to whom. **Relationship groups** (such as households) group clients. **Contact-contact relationships** link people, like a client and their accountant. **Account-account relationships** link businesses, like a company and its subsidiary. **Referrals** let staff pass a lead to the right expert, for example a teller passing a mortgage lead to a lender. **Intelligent need-based referrals** route referrals to the right person or queue based on the client's need, and referral scoring helps prioritise them.

blocks.heading: Action Plans for Client Lifecycle Management
blocks.body: **Action plans** are reusable checklists of tasks, built from **action plan templates**. They make sure common processes, like opening an account or onboarding a new client, are done the same way every time. Each task can have a due date based on the plan's start date and can be assigned to a role or user. Action plans can be attached to accounts, opportunities and other records, and progress can be tracked as tasks are completed.

blocks.heading: Rollup Summaries and Financial Aggregations
blocks.body: Advisers want to see totals, such as a client's total assets or a household's total deposits. FSC **rollups** add up balances from financial accounts to the people who own them and then to their households. Settings control whether joint accounts count for the primary owner only or for all owners. **Rollup by lookup (RBL)** rules define which fields and records are added up. Rollups can be recalculated in bulk after data loads. Without them, advisers would have to add up accounts by hand.

blocks.heading: Compliance, KYC, and Document Management
blocks.body: Financial firms must control who sees client data. **Compliant data sharing** lets you share financial accounts, opportunities and interactions only with the people who should see them, based on roles in a deal or client team, rather than opening up whole objects. **Interaction summaries** record meetings with clients and can be marked confidential. Firms also track identity checks for **Know Your Customer** rules and store required documents with clear review dates. Field audit history and event monitoring help show regulators who did what.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Financial Services Cloud Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions start with a client situation. Work out which records represent the people and money involved, then which feature acts on them.

blocks.heading: FSC Data Model Extensions
blocks.body: Use the standard FSC objects first. Financial account, role, holding, goal and asset or liability cover most needs.

blocks.heading: Client 360 & Relationship Manager
blocks.body: The client profile shows financial accounts, goals and relationships in one place, with rollup totals.

blocks.heading: Household & Relationship Management
blocks.body: Households group people through account-contact relationships. One member is primary.

blocks.heading: Insurance-Specific Features
blocks.body: Insurance policies, coverages and claims can be tracked for clients alongside their other financial accounts.

blocks.heading: Compliance & Audit Trail
blocks.body: Compliant data sharing limits access by role. Confidential interaction summaries hide meeting notes from others.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Financial Services Cloud:

sampleQuestions.question: A married couple and their adult son share some bank accounts. How should they be represented in FSC?
options: One single person account covering the whole of the family
Three person accounts linked to a household
sampleQuestions.explanation: Each person is a person account, and the household groups them while keeping each one's details separate.
whyWrong: An Opportunity is a deal, not a family.
One account for three people loses individual details.
Leads are for prospects, not clients.

sampleQuestions.question: A joint savings account is owned by two clients. What links the account to both people?
options: Financial account roles for each owner
A contact-to-contact relationship and nothing else
Two copies of the financial account
sampleQuestions.explanation: Financial account roles connect one financial account to each person, with their role such as joint owner.
whyWrong: Contact relationships link people, not accounts.

sampleQuestions.question: An adviser wants to see the total of all deposits for a family in one number. What feature provides this?
options: Rollups from financial accounts to the household
A custom formula field placed on each person record
A manual sum in a spreadsheet
sampleQuestions.explanation: FSC rollups add up balances from financial accounts to people and their household.
whyWrong: Formulas can't sum across related financial accounts.
A weekly email is not live data.

sampleQuestions.question: A bank teller learns a client wants a mortgage. How should the lead reach a mortgage specialist?
options: Send a Chatter post out to everyone in the whole bank
Create a referral that is routed to the mortgage team
sampleQuestions.explanation: Referrals pass leads to the right expert, and need-based routing sends them to the right person or queue.
whyWrong: Action plans are checklists, not referrals.
A broad post may be missed and isn't tracked.
Updating the address doesn't pass the lead.

sampleQuestions.question: Every new client must go through the same 12 onboarding steps. What should be used?
options: A newly created household for each step
An action plan template per new client
sampleQuestions.explanation: Action plan templates create the same set of tasks each time, with due dates and owners.
whyWrong: Goals track a client's savings targets.

sampleQuestions.question: A client's investment account holds shares in several funds. Where are the individual funds recorded?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Financial holdings record the securities or funds within an investment account.

sampleQuestions.question: A client owns a house and has a mortgage with another bank. How can the adviser record these?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Assets and liabilities record things owned or owed that aren't financial accounts at the firm.
whyWrong: Holdings are investments inside an account.

sampleQuestions.question: Only the advisers on a client's deal team should see that client's opportunities, without opening the object to everyone. What fits?
options: Compliant data sharing based on the team roles
Setting the org-wide default to Public Read/Write
sampleQuestions.explanation: Compliant data sharing grants access based on roles in the relationship or deal, which meets privacy needs.
whyWrong: Public access shows the data to everyone.

sampleQuestions.question: An adviser records notes from a sensitive meeting that other staff must not see. What should they use?
options: A field on the Account visible to all
An email to the whole branch
sampleQuestions.explanation: Interaction summaries record meetings and can be marked confidential to limit who can see them.
whyWrong: A field visible to all defeats the point.
A public post is visible to many people.
Emailing the branch spreads the notes.

sampleQuestions.question: A client's accountant should be linked to the client so advisers can see the connection. What should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Contact-contact relationships link people, such as a client and their adviser or accountant.
whyWrong: Households are for people managing money together.
Financial account roles link people to accounts.

sampleQuestions.question: After loading 50,000 financial accounts, household totals look wrong. What should the admin do?
options: Ask advisers to edit each account
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bulk recalculation updates rollup totals after large data loads.
whyWrong: Editing accounts one by one isn't practical.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants to save for their child's university fees over ten years. Which FSC record tracks this?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Financial goals track targets like education or retirement savings and progress toward them.

sampleQuestions.question: A subsidiary company should be linked to its parent company in FSC. What should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Account-account relationships link businesses, such as a parent and subsidiary.
whyWrong: Roles link people to financial accounts.

sampleQuestions.question: The firm must show it checked each client's identity under Know Your Customer rules. What should be recorded?
options: Identity checks and documents with dates and outcomes on the client record
Nothing at all, because KYC sits entirely outside Salesforce
sampleQuestions.explanation: Recording identity checks and documents with dates gives a clear audit trail for KYC.
whyWrong: Firms need evidence, wherever the check is done.
A post isn't a reliable record.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement about households in FSC is correct?
options: A household can only have one member
A household is a type of Lead
sampleQuestions.explanation: Households group people through account-contact relationships, with a primary member.
whyWrong: Financial accounts are still needed to hold balances.
